title: Retro Game QA test manifest
description: Versioned, human-reviewable description of a deterministic retro-game replay test. The manifest pins every input to the replay so that a CI machine can reproduce it with no model calls.

schema_version.description: Manifest schema version. The runner rejects any version it does not implement.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within a suite. Used for evidence paths.

description.description: One-line human summary of the behaviour under test.

target.description: The ROM under test and the console profile it must be replayed against.

rom.description: Path to the ROM, relative to the manifest file. Absolute paths are rejected.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the ROM. A mismatch is a hard failure: the runner must never replay against a different build.

region.description: Console region the trace was authored against. Region changes timing and is part of the pinned contract.

emulator.description: Emulator + core identity. Pinned so a trace cannot silently replay on a different core.

adapter.description: Adapter name. Only adapters the runner implements are accepted.

min_version.description: Minimum emulator version required (semver). The runner refuses an older binary.

initial_state.description: Machine state before frame 0. 'clean_boot' is a power-on reset from a zero-filled RAM; no savestate is loaded.

ports.description: Controller ports configuration. Port 1 is the only port the first adapter drives; declaring a device that is not a standard controller is an unsupported capability and is rejected.

trace.description: Frame-indexed controller trace. Each entry names the frame at which the given buttons begin to be held; the button set stays held until a later entry changes it. Buttons absent from an entry's 'held' list are released at that frame.

format.description: Trace format identifier. 'frame_events_v1' is the only supported format.

frames.description: Strictly increasing zero-based emulator frames, including reset/boot. inputPolled applies trace[F]; endFrame samples F. Empty held releases all buttons.

limits.description: Hard bounds so a replay always terminates.

max_frames.description: Maximum emulated frames to run. The runner stops here even if the trace is longer.

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock timeout for the whole emulator process.

checkpoints.description: Memory assertions evaluated at their named frame. Symbols are resolved from build artifacts at run time; an unresolvable symbol is a hard failure, never a silent default. Screenshot checkpoints are a distinct type and are not gameplay assertions.

screenshot_checkpoints.description: Visual baselines, kept distinct from gameplay assertions. Not supported by the headless adapter; declaring one fails loudly until a capture path is proven.

frame.description: Emulated frame at which the assertion is sampled, after that frame's vblank.

value.description: Required for binary comparisons; omitted for zero/nonzero.

span.description: Byte width of the observation (1 or 2). 2 is little-endian.

symbol_assertion.description: Assertion against a named symbol resolved from a linker label map, relative to a segment base.

symbol.description: Label name as it appears in the linker map (e.g. pad1_held).

symbols_from.description: Linker label map to resolve the symbol from. Path relative to the manifest. Required for symbol assertions so addresses are never inferred.

segment_base.description: Explicit relocation addend. Use 0 for absolute ld65 -Ln labels; nonzero only for genuinely relative maps.

address_assertion.description: Assertion against an explicit CPU memory address, used when no symbol is available.

baseline.description: Approved baseline image, relative to the manifest.
